Online I constantly hear people talking about how MMOs in general are no longer fun and that all new MMOs are, without exception, absolute shit. I was watching this video by Boogie2988 earlier and in it he mentioned in passing that the MMO industry simply isn't as profitable as it used to be and likely won't be again for a long time, as if that were something everyone knows already. The MMO genre has certainly evolved quite a lot since WoW's peak years ago (monetization-wise if not gameplay-wise) yet I haven't seen any numbers to back up the assertion that the genre itself is dying. Is the death of the MMO genre currently taking place, or is that just an exaggeration by people who no longer have any interest in playing MMOs for one reason or another?
Is the death of the MMO genre exaggerated?

I dont think that the genre is dieing, more the idea of AAA themepark titles with huge budgets coming along and grabbing millions of concurrent subscribers is dieing, as is the idea of ftp MMOs being long -term profitable.

However I think we will/are seeing a resurgance of more niche products that will get 50-100k subscribers, and a more open world feel. Similar to the way vanilla wow/EQ were, but with some of the lessons from the last decade and a half applied to them. Black Desert Online is one upcoming game that I have my eye on in this regard, if it is done right, I think it could really do well. There are obviously a largish group of players that want to support a MMO of this nature, they just want the game to not be utter shit/get wreaked by the publisher - see Archeage.

I am actually more hopeful about the state of the MMO market moving forwards then I have been in some years.

Disclaimer - I am still playing WoW, purely to raid.
The money it takes to create a MMO apparently is making investors shy away from new ideas, and rehashing old formulas from more succesful MMOs hasn't worked the last 2000 times.
This could be partially true for MMOs popular in 'the west', but I don't think they decline at all in the eastern countries.

People enjoy saying that something is dying. It wasn't long ago that we were being sold the idea that PC gaming was dying. In a politically-fueled move over GamerGate, we just had a bunch of major publications proclaim that "gamers" were dead. Stating the "death" of something in an industry like this, where old patterns, such as retro 2D platformers, are rarely abandoned, tends to fall in line with some sort of agenda.

The fact is, we've been given a few great entries in the MMO world in the past few years. I recall enjoying Tera, Rift, and Guild Wars 2 is still fantastic (if poorly-executed in terms of late-game content). A lot of people love/loved Wildstar and ESO. We shouldn't discount the genre as failing.

I think that the western MMO genre is certainly dying, while the asian side of it is growing and thriving. The west gets the rare few Korean or what have you MMO ported over here and it either crashes and burns in the first few months or thrives for about a year before dying (typically because it refuses to adapt to west standards.)

I've played EQ, GW, DaoC, LoTRo, and WOW. All of the current offerings are repeating the sins of their fathers. They were all fun, but they turned into endgame raiding that is over time consuming. They all got stuck focusing on the the highest level content, under developing starter regions. They all hit their caps and turned to alternate (gimmicky) ways to progress (item customization, custom class options, etc.). Offering PvP as an endgame options is super tricky to balance, and often overly traumatic to new characters.

I don't think the genre is going away, but people are getting burned out on the same mechanics and fundamental problems. Some of the smaller offerings can afford to think outside the current box, but without large numbers of players, they can't develop content at the rate the larger games can.

I think it is heavilly exaggerated. Here's why:

  • World of Warcraft: Last I recall right after launching their latest expansion in the US they had ten million subscribers. That's 10,000,000 * 14 each month which nets at the very least 140,000,000 each month.

  • Eve Online: Last I recall, 0.5 Million active subs at the same price so at the very least 7,000,000 a month however you should also account for PLEX purchases which is a very integral part of the game. I'm not sure how to go about calculating that but I'm sure someone more intelligent than me could.

  • Star Wars the Old Republic: Is an MMO being produced by EA. Since EA doesn't release any numbers I'm just going to guess but since it is still getting expansions and regular updates I would say it is profitable. If it wasn't I would guess its life support would have been cut a long time ago.

  • Currently in active development, we have Everquest Landmark and Everyquest Next. Both highly anticipated and looked forward to.

We also have ArchAge, Guild Wars 2, Rift, and probably a few more modern MMOs that I'm forgetting so as you can see the MMO genre is nowhere near dead I believe it is purely opinion that the genre is dying. Remember that CCP was/is making enough money from a single game to support development of another MMO, and FPS, and Oculus space fighter game, a "dead" game, and it's "military grade servers".

I just think that the genre, for a lot of people, just hasn't changed much in the past decade to the point that it's like playing the same game with a slightly different skin and feel to it.

I reckon when something actually good that makes some REAL changes (not just adding the most liked features from mods and other MMOs) then it will pick up again.

I think it will need a game like Star Citizen to give the genre a nice kick up the ass and bring the MMO back to the forefront.
